notes: Other: On 15 February 2024, Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Meshal al-Ahmad al-Sabah issued a decree to dissolve the National Assembly (coded to capital Kuwait city). The decree cited a violation of constitutional principles, including using 'offensive and inappropriate' language. The decree came one day after the cabinet boycotted a parliamentary session in objection to a speech delivered by an MP a week earlier, which cabinet ministers interpreted to be disrespectful to the Emir. The parliament had already been dissolved in April 2023 as part of a years-long political deadlock in the country.

Other: On 21 February 2024, the Kuwaiti government issued a decree to temporarily suspend the National Assembly's election law until 1 October 2024 (coded to capital Kuwait City). The government also reissued the old elections law to allow for holding snap elections within two months. The decree prohibits voters who have been convicted of felonies, crimes against honor or trust, or a crime of insulting the divine entity, the prophets, or the Emir from voting in the upcoming 2024 elections unless rehabilitated. Kuwait's Emir dissolved the parliament on 15 February 2024. Elections for the new parliament are expected to take place on 13 April 2024.

Other: On 29 February 2024, Kuwait's Court of Cassation issued a ruling that formally outlawed Hezbollah and Al Ashtar Brigades (coded to capital Kuwait City). It criminalized joining or cooperating with the two groups, labeling them as 'forbidden and criminal' groups and accusing them of 'planning to destabilize Kuwait to establish an Iranian-style republic'. The ruling overturned the acquittal of 3 Kuwaitis and a Lebanese citizen, convicting them of espionage for Hezbollah and Bahrain's Al Ashtar Brigades. An appeals court had previously acquitted the defendants after being charged with funding Hezbollah-affiliated entities on the basis that Kuwait has not formally outlawed Hezbollah.

Security measures: On 3 March 2024, Bahraini police forces closed all roads to Erada Square in Kuwait City (Al Asimah) to prevent a scheduled protest in solidarity with the Palestinian people in the context of the latest round of violence in Israel-Palestine. Kuwait's interior ministry emphasized a ban on 'unauthorized assembly,' including marches and calls for gatherings on social media platforms.
